symptom: my daemon-driven GPIO script fails on the new Pi 5. It opens the pigpio daemon socket and gets 'socket connect failed' / no GPIO access.

files.app.py:
import pigpio
pi = pigpio.pi()
pi.set_mode(17, pigpio.OUTPUT)
pi.write(17, 1)
pi.stop()

gold.diagnosis: The pigpio daemon (pigpiod) drives BCM283x mmio registers directly and is broken on the Pi 5, whose GPIO is on the RP1 southbridge exposed via /dev/gpiochipN. Only lgpio works natively. Rewrite using gpiozero, which auto-selects lgpio on the Pi 5.
